questions.question: What is the lesson's core invariant for video generation?
options: Every frame must be identical.
A subject should change only when the intended action, camera plan, or shot boundary calls for it, not because state drifted accidentally.
The video must use the highest available frame rate.
A text prompt must determine every pixel and motion vector.
questions.explanation: Controlled continuity distinguishes intended change from accidental drift across frames, windows, and shots.

questions.question: A six-second clip is generated at 12 frames per second. How many frames does the generator create before optional interpolation?
questions.explanation: Frame count is duration multiplied by generated frame rate: 6 x 12 = 72 frames.

questions.question: Why do overlapping temporal windows help a production system?
options: They remove the need for evaluation.
They provide shared boundary state and a bounded retry unit for long clips.
They guarantee that rights are cleared.
They make service time independent of duration.
questions.explanation: Overlap carries continuity evidence across windows and lets the system retry a failed region plus its seam instead of restarting the whole clip.

questions.question: Which condition most directly separates subject movement from viewpoint movement?
options: A camera trajectory stored separately from subject motion controls
A larger object-storage bucket
A lower safety threshold
A random retry seed
questions.explanation: Separate camera and subject controls make generation intent and evaluation contracts more precise.

questions.question: A model's average quality improves, but the required identity-after-occlusion slice falls below its floor. What should the release gate do?
options: Release because the aggregate score improved.
Remove the difficult slice from the report.
Block promotion until the required identity slice passes or an explicit bounded exception is approved.
Replace quality evaluation with GPU utilization.
questions.explanation: Critical slice floors prevent aggregate metrics from hiding user-visible or safety-relevant regressions.

questions.question: What does a valid C2PA Content Credential establish by itself?
options: That every depicted event happened in the real world
That signed provenance assertions are bound to the asset and can be validated for tampering and trust
That all training and output rights are legally cleared
That output moderation is unnecessary
questions.explanation: Provenance records origin and history assertions. Truth, safety, consent, and rights remain separate decisions.

questions.question: Why should capacity planning use measured service time for each generation profile?
options: All video jobs have the same compute cost.
Duration, resolution, frames, steps, model behavior, decoding, and evaluation create different service-time distributions.
Measured service time removes queueing completely.
It guarantees that no worker will fail.
questions.explanation: Profiles convert heterogeneous media requests into measured resource demand that admission control and scheduling can use.

questions.question: Which metric best exposes wasted generation and post-processing work?
options: GPU utilization alone
Raw submitted jobs
Cost per released second, broken down by retries, blocks, and abandoned previews
The number of prompt characters
questions.explanation: Cost per released second includes work that never becomes a usable asset and makes retry or rejection waste visible.
